sign: Three terraces, one well, too many ladders.

lines: Keeper Ysolde: Sit under the willow and drink from the pool. It mends tired Spirlings.
Trader Ebbe: Brook-cooled tonics, fresh every day.
trader.action: shop tonic strong_tonic remedy dry_towel cooling_gel kin_charm revival_leaf pruning_shears grounding_rod smelling_salts

lines: Ropemaker Nell: The old wells hereabouts go deep. You'll want a ladder you can leave behind.
Ropemaker Nell: Tie it where you see a chalk mark. It holds.
Ropemaker Nell: Every knot I tie has a name. That one was 'Patience'.
Old Bertil: Orrin guards that well like someone would steal it. Who'd steal a hole?

kid: Wren-kid: I counted the ladder rungs. All of them. Two hundred and six!

lines: Driver Fenna: Valley Coach, Wrenhollow stop. Climb in, the seats are dry.
Weaver Tamsa: I weave all day so I have something to do with my hands while Lise talks to her goats about me.
Weaver Tamsa: My threads stopped tangling by themselves. Strange how a Rift reaches so far.
Well-Keeper Orrin: Everyone here mocks me. The well is the only one who listens, and it just echoes.
Well-Keeper Orrin: The well water tastes of nothing again. That's how it should taste.
Goatherd Lise: My goats are smarter than Orrin. At least they leave the well when nothing happens.
Goatherd Lise: The goats climb up to the rim again. They hated the Rift more than I did.
Fiddler Brann: I play loud at night so nobody hears Tamsa gossip. It doesn't work. Nothing drowns her out.
Fiddler Brann: My fiddle stays in tune all night now. A small miracle, but mine.
Basket-Maker Ilse: Brann calls it music. The goats call it a warning.
Basket-Maker Ilse: The reeds by the fen stand straight again. Better baskets for everyone.
An old cartographer's stone. A compass rose is cut into it, worn almost smooth.
Surveyor Ilka: A map is only as good as what you've looked at. Here, look further.
Surveyor Ilka: Face where you want to look and press A on open ground. Give the glass a breath between looks.
Surveyor Ilka: Six steps out, no further. Past that, even glass gets lazy.
Well-Keeper Orrin: She said WHAT? Here, coins. Don't tell the goats.
